when.quote: When a customer needs to file a formal dispute for a credit card transaction (such as unauthorized charges, merchant issues, or billing errors), the agent must gather comprehensive information and call the file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_4829 tool.

starts.note: customer: start only when the customer asks to dispute a credit card charge. Never file a dispute the customer did not ask for. Order a replacement card only if the customer asks for the card to be cancelled and replaced. Provisional credit is never a separate action: it is decided for each dispute and passed in that dispute's eligible_for_provisional_credit flag. If the customer also asked for something else in the same conversation (for example a credit limit increase), do the requests in the order the customer gave them, and verify only once.
starts.quote: However, if you've already tried contacting the merchant without success, or if the charge appears to be fraudulent, please don't hesitate to reach out to us right away.

tools.not_used: Not used in this job. Provisional credit is recorded only through the dispute's eligible_for_provisional_credit flag. No dispute document says to post a statement credit when a dispute is filed. This tool is for goodwill credits, fee reversals and similar adjustments, and for credits after a dispute is resolved.

steps.do: Read the dispute history once, in check_dispute_history, and count the disputes dated in the past 12 months, measured against get_time. Add 1 to the count for each dispute filed successfully earlier in this conversation. Before each filing, use this running count for the previous-disputes criterion: the dispute meets it only if the count is 2 or less.

steps.do: Decide eligible_for_provisional_credit using the Provisional Credit Eligibility Guidelines. Every criterion must hold: (1) The account has been open at least 60 days (open date from get_accounts compared with get_time). (2) The reason is unauthorized_fraudulent_charge or duplicate_charge, or it is goods_services_not_received with the purchase made more than 30 days ago. (3) The amount is at least $25.00 and no more than the maximum for the tier of the card the transaction is on. (4) No more than 2 disputes in the past 12 months (check_dispute_history, or running_dispute_count when several disputes are filed). (5) For a reason other than fraud, the merchant was contacted. If any criterion fails, set it to false.
steps.quote: 15. eligible_for_provisional_credit (boolean) - Agent must determine this based on the Provisional Credit Eligibility Guidelines article in this knowledge base. Pass true or false.

steps.do: Ask which of the disputes the customer most wants handled first, unless they have already said. Do not explain the internal eligibility rules.

steps.quote: 4. Previous Disputes: The customer has not filed more than 2 disputes in the past 12 months

steps.do: Set the filing order. First file the disputes that meet criteria (1), (2), (3) and (5), starting with the ones the customer named as most important (ask_priority). Then file all the other disputes. Before each filing, recompute criterion (4) from running_dispute_count and set that dispute's eligible_for_provisional_credit again.

rules.rule: Provisional credit is true only if ALL of these hold: (1) the account has been open at least 60 days; (2) the reason is unauthorized_fraudulent_charge or duplicate_charge, or it is goods_services_not_received with the purchase made more than 30 days ago; (3) the amount is at least $25.00 and no more than the tier maximum; (4) no more than 2 disputes in the past 12 months; (5) for a non-fraud dispute, the merchant was contacted first
rules.quote: ## Eligibility Criteria — Customer is ELIGIBLE for provisional credit if ALL of the following are true:

rules.rule: The reasons incorrect_amount, goods_services_not_as_described, canceled_subscription_still_charging and refund_never_processed are never eligible for provisional credit
rules.quote: - Dispute reason is 'incorrect_amount', 'goods_services_not_as_described', 'canceled_subscription_still_charging', or 'refund_never_processed'

rules.rule: Mid-tier cards (Silver Rewards, Business Silver Rewards, Green Rewards, Silver Zoom) have a provisional credit maximum of $5000.00. Other tiers: Entry $2500, Premium $10000, Elite $15000, Diamond Elite $25000.
rules.quote: - Mid Tier (Silver Rewards Card, Business Silver Rewards Card, Green Rewards Card, Silver Zoom Card): Maximum $5000.00

rules.rule: Entry-tier cards (Bronze Rewards, EcoCard, Business Bronze Rewards, Crypto-Cash Back) have a provisional credit maximum of $2500.00
rules.quote: Entry Tier (Bronze Rewards Card, EcoCard, Business Bronze Rewards Card, Crypto-Cash Back Card): Maximum $2500.00

rules.rule: Premium-tier cards (Gold Rewards, Business Gold Rewards) have a provisional credit maximum of $10000.00
rules.quote: Premium Tier (Gold Rewards Card, Business Gold Rewards Card): Maximum $10000.00

rules.rule: Elite-tier cards (Platinum Rewards, Business Platinum Rewards) have a provisional credit maximum of $15000.00
rules.quote: Elite Tier (Platinum Rewards Card, Business Platinum Rewards Card): Maximum $15000.00

rules.rule: The Invitation-tier card (Diamond Elite) has a provisional credit maximum of $25000.00
rules.quote: Invitation Tier (Diamond Elite Card): Maximum $25000.00

jobs.done_when: All of the following hold. The customer is verified and the verification is logged. file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_4829 has been called successfully once for each confirmed transaction in the records, on every card involved, with all required arguments. Each call carries that card's last 4 digits and the customer's card_action for that card, plus an eligible_for_provisional_credit value decided for that dispute, using the running dispute count and the order from the customer's priorities when several disputes are filed. If the customer chose cancel_and_reissue and was eligible, a replacement was ordered. Charges not found in the records were explained and not disputed. The customer has been told that each dispute is filed and whether provisional credit applies. If filing failed, the failure has been explained instead and a transfer offered. If the customer raised another request, the agent has moved on to that job without verifying again.

when.quote: This document outlines the step-by-step workflow for agents to process CLI requests, including verification and final decision. These steps MUST be followed in the exact order listed.

starts.note: customer: start only when the account owner or an authorized account manager asks to raise the credit limit on a credit card. No document says the agent may offer an increase without being asked. If a request is denied and the customer asks again in the same conversation (for example after paying the balance down), that is a new customer request: run the resubmit steps. If the customer was already verified earlier in this conversation (for example in a dispute job), do not verify again.
starts.quote: Only the account owner or an authorized account manager may submit a CLI request for the account.

tools.not_used: The CLI job never orders a replacement card. The replacement tier document is cited only to map cards to tiers, and a pending replacement only blocks the CLI.
No CLI document names a tool for the customer to run. The agent submits, checks and decides the request itself.

The CLI job never moves money. If the customer asks to pay the balance down from checking after a high_utilization denial, that is the separate job paying_off_credit_card_balance_from_checking_account.
The CLI job reads no bank accounts. Only the separate payment job uses it to find the checking account.

steps.do: Check every criterion, in this order, using get_current_time for the dates. (1) Account age ≥ 120/90/60 days (Entry/Mid/Premium) from the open date. (2) Cooldown: no APPROVED prior request within 120/90/60 days; ignore the request just submitted and any denied ones. (3) No dispute with status open or under_review on this card. (4) No replacement order in a non-final state (pending or shipped). (5) No past-due balance. (6) Utilization = balance ÷ limit, strictly below 70%/80%/90%. (7) Consecutive on-time payments for the required months: 6 (Entry) or 3 (Mid/Premium). (8) Amount within the tier maximum.

steps.do: Step 5: tell the customer the decision. For an approval, give the new total limit. open_questions: When a customer asks for a dispute and then a credit limit increase, the dispute just filed is active, so the CLI check 'No Pending Disputes' denies the increase with 'pending_disputes'. No document says whether to warn the customer before submitting, or to change the order the customer asked for. This workflow keeps the customer's order and explains the denial afterwards.

The CLI documents define only the Entry, Mid and Premium tiers. Platinum/Business Platinum (Elite) and Diamond Elite (Invitation) are treated as 'Premium-tier and above' from the replacement document.

Step 3 of the CLI processing document ('Verify Payment History and Requested Amount') has no body. Payment history and the amount maximum are taken from doc_credit_cards_credit_card_account_logistics_006.
No document names the field in the account or payment records that shows a past-due balance.
deny_credit_limit_increase_5848 takes one reason. When several criteria fail, the documents do not say which to record; this workflow uses the first one in the document's order.
No document says whether a second dispute may be filed on a transaction that already has an open dispute.

steps.do: Get the verified user's credit card accounts (fresh read) for the card's id, type, current credit limit, balance and open date.
steps.quote: This can be found by calling get_credit_card_accounts_by_user.

steps.do: Find the card tier (Entry: Bronze Rewards, EcoCard, Business Bronze; Mid: Silver Rewards, Business Silver, Green Rewards, Silver Zoom; Premium: Gold, Business Gold and above) and compare the requested increase with the maximum: Entry 25%, Mid 50%, Premium 50% of the current limit. If it is above the maximum, tell the customer the maximum they can request and ask whether to go ahead with that amount. Do not submit until the customer confirms an amount within the limit.
steps.quote: BEFORE submitting any CLI request, verify that the customer's requested increase amount is within the maximum allowed for their card tier.

steps.do: Unlock submit_credit_limit_increase_request_7392, then call it through call_discoverable_agent_tool. This records the request before the eligibility checks; it is not an approval, so do not tell the customer it is approved.

args.requested_increase_amount: integer dollar increase confirmed in check_amount_within_max (new limit minus current limit)

steps.if: the customer has confirmed an increase amount that is within the tier maximum
steps.quote: Once the customer has confirmed a valid increase amount within their tier's limits, submit the request on their behalf using the submit_credit_limit_increase_request_7392 tool.

steps.do: Get the current time to compute account age and the cooldown.
steps.quote: 1. Account Age: Verify the account has been open for the minimum required days for their card tier.

steps.do: Unlock and call get_credit_limit_increase_history_4829.
steps.quote: 2. Cooldown Period: Use the get_credit_limit_increase_history_4829 tool to check if the customer has submitted a request within the cooldown period for their card tier.

steps.do: Unlock (if not already unlocked) and call get_user_dispute_history_7291 to read active disputes on this account.
steps.quote: 3. No Pending Disputes: Verify the account has no active disputes.

steps.do: Unlock and call get_pending_replacement_orders_5765.
steps.quote: 4. No Pending Replacement Cards: Verify there are no outstanding replacement card orders for this account.

steps.do: Unlock and call get_payment_history_6183 with months by tier: Entry 6, Mid 3, Premium 3.

args.months: 6 for Entry-tier, 3 for Mid-tier or Premium-tier

steps.quote: Use the get_payment_history_6183 tool to verify the customer's payment history meets the requirement for their card tier.

steps.do: Check every criterion before deciding. (a) Account age at least Entry 120 / Mid 90 / Premium 60 days (open date vs current time). (b) Cooldown: no approved request in the last 120 / 90 / 60 days, not counting the request submitted in submit_cli; denied requests do not count. (c) No active (open/under_review) dispute on this account. (d) No replacement order that is not delivered or cancelled. (e) Account current with no past-due balance. (f) Utilization (balance / limit) below 70% / 80% / 90%. (g) Consecutive on-time payment months meet 6 / 3 / 3. (h) Amount within the tier maximum. Record the first criterion that fails, in this order.
steps.quote: You MUST check ALL of the following eligibility criteria before making an approval or denial decision as this ensures complete audit records.

steps.do: Unlock and call approve_credit_limit_increase_5847 to apply the new limit.

args.new_credit_limit: current limit from cli_get_accounts plus the confirmed increase

steps.if: decide_cli found every criterion met and the amount within limits
steps.quote: 1. Use the approve_credit_limit_increase_5847 tool to approve and apply the increase.

steps.do: Unlock and call deny_credit_limit_increase_5848 with the reason for the first failed criterion: insufficient_account_age, cooldown_period_active, pending_disputes, pending_replacement_card, past_due_balance, high_utilization, insufficient_payment_history, requested_amount_exceeds_limit, or other.
steps.if: decide_cli found any criterion not met
steps.quote: 1. Use the deny_credit_limit_increase_5848 tool to record the denial.

steps.do: Tell the customer the decision. If approved, confirm the new credit limit. If denied, explain the reason and when they may reapply (for example, after the dispute is resolved, the replacement is delivered or cancelled, the cooldown ends, or utilization falls below the threshold).
steps.quote: Inform the customer of the decision and provide next steps. For approvals, confirm the new credit limit. For denials, explain the reason and when they may be eligible to reapply.

rules.rule: Never submit a request above the tier maximum
rules.quote: Do NOT submit a request that exceeds the tier limit.

rules.rule: Maximum increase per request: Entry 25%, Mid 50%, Premium 50% of the current limit
rules.quote: Mid-tier cards: Maximum increase of 50% of current credit limit per request.

rules.rule: Entry-tier maximum increase is 25%
rules.quote: Entry-tier cards: Maximum increase of 25% of current credit limit per request.

rules.rule: If the request is above the maximum, offer the maximum and ask whether to go ahead
rules.quote: If the customer requests more than the maximum allowed for their tier, inform them of the maximum amount they are eligible for and ask if they would like to proceed with that amount instead.

rules.rule: Submit before checking eligibility
rules.quote: Eligibility checks are internal and not exposed to customers, so the submission must happen first.

rules.rule: Account age minimum: Entry 120, Mid 90, Premium 60 days; qualifies on the day the minimum is reached
rules.quote: You qualify on or after the day the minimum is reached.

rules.rule: Cooldown (Entry 120 / Mid 90 / Premium 60 days) applies only after an approved request
rules.quote: This applies only if your most recent request was approved. Denied requests do not trigger a cooldown period.

rules.rule: Within the cooldown, deny and say when the customer may reapply
rules.quote: If a request exists within this period, deny the new request and inform the customer when they will be eligible to submit again.

rules.rule: Utilization must be strictly below Entry 70% / Mid 80% / Premium 90%
rules.quote: Utilization at or above the threshold does not qualify.

rules.rule: Mid-tier needs 3 consecutive on-time months (Entry 6, Premium 3)
rules.quote: Mid-tier cards: Requires 3 consecutive months of on-time payments.

rules.rule: Any active dispute on the account, including one filed earlier in this conversation, blocks approval (denial_reason 'pending_disputes')
rules.quote: 3. No Pending Disputes: Verify the account has no active disputes.

rules.rule: Any replacement order not delivered or cancelled counts as pending
rules.quote: Treat the account as having pending replacement activity unless every order is clearly delivered or cancelled.

rules.rule: Account must be current with no past-due balance
rules.quote: 5. Account Good Standing: The account must be current with no past-due balance.

rules.rule: Tier mapping: Mid-tier = Silver Rewards, Business Silver Rewards, Green Rewards, Silver Zoom
rules.quote: Mid-tier (Silver Rewards Card, Business Silver Rewards Card, Green Rewards Card, Silver Zoom Card): $10.00.

rules.rule: Allowed denial reasons
rules.quote: denial_reason (string, required): Must be one of: 'insufficient_account_age', 'cooldown_period_active', 'pending_disputes', 'pending_replacement_card', 'past_due_balance', 'high_utilization', 'insufficient_payment_history', 'requested_amount_exceeds_limit', 'other'.

draft.done_when: A within-limit request was submitted, every eligibility check was read from its tool, exactly one of approve_credit_limit_increase_5847 or deny_credit_limit_increase_5848 was called, and the customer was told the decision (new limit, or denial reason and when to reapply).
